page: Amazon Web Services i4g.xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 4 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 architecture, utilizing the AWS Neoverse-N1 model running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 937 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance operates on the Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average performance in stress-ng single-core (1520.08) and multi-core (6056.47) CPU tests. Large block memory bandwidth is also average, with 71.67 GB/sec read and 34.86 GB/sec write speeds. However, the instance exhibits weak performance in several areas, including small block memory bandwidth (236.01 GB/sec), single-threaded gzip compression (20.3 GB/sec), and Geekbench multi-core (3224.0). Poor performance is observed in Passmark CPU encryption (541.67) and LLM inference processing, where a 135M model achieves 125.16 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 26.64 tokens/sec for text generation.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the i4g.xlarge offers a high density of local NVMe SSD storage paired with a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, making it a viable option for storage-intensive workloads that do not require high-performance compute. The hardware profile is suited for database operations, local caching, and storage-heavy applications where high IOPS and local capacity are prioritized over raw CPU execution speed or cryptographic performance.
